EMG-10.name: The Endgame Configuration (nine simultaneous conditions)
EMG-10.one_line: The campaign's ending state is defined not by a single victory condition but by how many of nine independently-achieved conditions across different systems are true at once, evaluated at an unspecified moment with no named mechanism for performing the check.
EMG-10.ends_when: UNCLEAR whether this case "ends" at all as a discrete event — the source frames it as a standing description of what a satisfying ending looks like, not a triggered check; absent a named evaluation moment, the most honest reading is that it never formally concludes on its own within the mechanics as described.
who_acts: the accumulated effect of many prior arcs (condition 2)
a faction's or player's deliberate action across one of several named paths (condition 3)
the avoidance of triggers by many different actors over the whole campaign (condition 8)
a specific ritual attempt's roll (condition 9) — no single actor controls the checklist as a whole

rows.need: nine named conditions, each belonging to a different subsystem (a person's perceptual development, a public knowledge-state, a succession outcome, a loyalty-track outcome, a world-health band, two separate clock thresholds, a private counter's value, and a ritual's success grade), must each be independently trackable as true or false at any given moment.
the game must be able to evaluate "at least three of nine," "all nine," and "none of nine" as distinct, meaningfully different outcomes, each with its own described consequence.

at least one of the nine conditions (a private counter reaching a floor) must be achievable only by never letting more than a small number of its underlying triggers fire across the entire campaign, since that counter is stated elsewhere in this corpus to never decrement.
a specific evaluation moment (a season, a triggering event, or a continuous check) at which the nine conditions are read together must exist.

the ritual-outcome condition must specify which of that ritual's several named success grades counts as satisfying the endgame checklist, since the same ritual is elsewhere given multiple distinct success grades with different effects.

EMG-11.name: 'Throughline resolution' — closing cross-system design-integration gaps
EMG-11.one_line: This document's "throughlines" are ten open integration questions between rules systems, not story arcs, closed by a single canonical patch — a different, unrelated use of the word "throughline" from the rest of this corpus, where it means how a narrative arc concludes.
EMG-11.ends_when: each of the ten questions is marked resolved by this document, except one (a pending mechanical spec for rank dismissal) and one (a cross-reference dependency on a separate stress test) which are explicitly left open pending future work — so the case as a whole does not fully end here.
who_acts: the design/editorial process itself (identifies the ten integration questions via a post-commit audit)
a named human authority (the document states its resolutions were approved by name)

rows.need: when multiple independent progress-clocks are scheduled to change state in the same accounting step, a fixed, named order of resolution must be applied — one category of event fully resolving before the next begins — rather than resolving them simultaneously or in an undefined order.

a finite, per-location capacity must be able to gate a character's rank advancement, such that reaching the qualifying rank with no capacity available produces a distinct, named provisional state rather than either blocking the advancement outright or granting it for free.

the game must be able to track a large but bounded set of named individual characters at different levels of tracked detail, and move a character between those levels automatically based on elapsed time, or manually on request.
a sub-track's operating cost must be able to scale with a separate, already-existing clock's value without requiring a brand-new clock to be introduced for that sub-track specifically.

a rank ladder must be able to be deliberately left without ranks at its top end, by design, for a thematic reason rather than an unfinished-spec reason, and the game must represent "no rank exists here on purpose" distinctly from "not yet specified."
a unique identifier scheme for individually-resolved design/editorial items must guarantee that two different resolved items never share the same identifier.

NPC-088.name: Carin Vedel
NPC-088.one_line: A copyist with no institutional position who hand-reproduces suppressed Einhir cultural texts -- the lowest-agency case in the roster.
NPC-088.ends_when: never automatically -- only by discovery, arrest, or death, or by a player-driven resolution; the source names no natural conclusion.
who_acts: any Church Inquisitor investigating the region
Restoration Movement leadership, insofar as they decide whether to protect or use her

rows.need: A person holding no office, post, or command must be able to perform a repeated, multi-week task (copying a text) that the engine tracks as ongoing work-in-progress with a start and an end, not only as a single instantaneous action.
The physical product of her labor (a copied text) must be able to exist as a persistent object that can be found, carried, hidden, given away, or destroyed independently of her.
Simply possessing the product of her labor must be able to trigger consequences for whoever holds it, independent of whether the act of copying was ever observed.
Her work must be able to accumulate institutional attention gradually across multiple undiscovered seasons, not only through a single detected incident.
A person with no faction rank, no assigned Duty, and no tracked Standing must still be able to generate a scene opportunity that brings a player into contact with her.

UNCLEAR: whether the texts she copies are ordinary suppressed-but-mundane cultural material or Thread-substrate content of the kind described elsewhere as legible only above a Thread Sensitivity threshold -- the source never states which, and a non-sensitive copyist's ability to faithfully reproduce either category is not the same.

A person with no political voice must be able to become personally significant -- worth a scene, worth a decision -- purely through the discovered effect of her private labor, without her ever taking a public political action herself.

Her season must be able to end through means that require no institutional process at all -- being found and killed, or simply vanishing -- not only through an arrest, trial, or faction-tree escalation.

The engine must represent something about a season of her life beyond identity-only reference data -- some tracked state that a player interaction can actually change -- for at least the season in which she is engaged.

A single scene of investigation, discovery, or protection involving her must be able to permanently change a persistent fact about her (protected / exposed / arrested / dead) that carries forward into subsequent seasons.

NPC-087.name: Uwe Askeland
NPC-087.one_line: A hedge-school teacher running illegal Einhir education in the southwest, holding no post beyond the classroom he keeps hidden.
NPC-087.ends_when: never automatically; only via a discovery-driven resolution (protect/report/leverage), or unremarked continuation.
who_acts: any Church or Crown authority present in the southwest territory

rows.need: A person with no office must be able to run a recurring, location-bound activity whose ongoing existence -- not any single completed task -- is itself the thing at stake.

The material he teaches must be classified as suppressed cultural/political knowledge, retainable by ordinary non-sensitive minds, rather than Thread-substrate knowledge subject to the setting's epistemological barrier.

The cumulative effect of many small private teaching sessions must be able to aggregate into a settlement- or territory-scale outcome without Askeland himself possessing the faction-level resources that the only named aggregation mechanism for this kind of cultural effect requires.

His discovery must be able to branch three ways for whoever finds him -- protect him, report him, or leverage the discovery -- with materially different consequences down each path, not just a binary helped/not-helped outcome.
A student's exposure (being caught attending, or found to have been taught) must be trackable as a consequence for the student, separate from any consequence for Askeland.
He must be reachable by a scene opportunity despite holding no faction Standing, no assigned Duty, and no Disposition floor with any faction leader.

His activity must be able to persist across seasons completely unwitnessed, and be discoverable later exactly as it would have been discovered earlier -- not silently resolved off-screen the way an unattended faction-generated opportunity is.

UNCLEAR: whether institutional attention toward his activity accumulates through the same channel used for Thread-heresy detection, given that what he teaches (per the need above) may be a caste/political offense rather than a metaphysical one.

NPC-086.name: Joren Bergvall
NPC-086.one_line: A Guild surveyor holding a technical, non-leadership office who has assembled physical evidence that a political conspiracy is actually a Calamity-caused blockage.
NPC-086.ends_when: never explicitly stated; presumably when the conspiracy narrative is durably dispelled or the data is destroyed or discredited.
who_acts: Guild leadership (whether they let him publish or suppress)
the faction whose founding narrative the data threatens

rows.need: A technical specialist's field data must be able to exist as a persistent evidence object with its own scope and quality, independent of any single Contest roll -- something that can be examined, copied, corroborated, or suppressed as an artifact.

Presenting his evidence to a political audience must be able to change what that audience believes about the cause of the sea-route blockage, and that changed belief must persist and spread to third parties who never saw the data themselves.

UNCLEAR: whether the causal fact his evidence supports (the blockage is Calamity-caused, not political) is itself Thread-substrate knowledge subject to the setting's epistemological barrier -- if so, a non-sensitive audience cannot stably retain the correct explanation even after being shown the evidence.

A Guild employee below faction-leadership rank must be reachable by a scene opportunity through his technical output becoming relevant to a player, not only through his faction leadership's own political business.
His findings must be able to be suppressed, altered, or bought before reaching a political audience, by an actor with an interest in the conspiracy narrative persisting.

His personal risk for holding or publishing this data must be trackable as politically motivated, distinct from the Church-heresy detection machinery that governs most other exposure risk in the setting.
Corroborating or refuting his claim must be possible for a third party through independent fieldwork, not only by taking his word for it.

NPC-075.name: Orm
NPC-075.one_line: The second-ranking Warden at the dying Southernmost outpost, thirty-one years into an unrewarded war of attrition against the Calamity's aftermath, answering to no faction.
NPC-075.ends_when: his death (possibly a deliberate death-in-service act), the outpost's fall, or -- per the sourcing gap above -- an undefined further state.
who_acts: every faction whose Thread-disruptive activity anywhere on the peninsula adds to his burden
the player, if and when access to the outpost is earned

rows.need: A person's decision to continue an exhausting, unrewarded maintenance labor (repairing breaches in the world's substrate) must be represented as a real season-to-season choice, including the possibility that he stops, burns out, or dies at it.

A practitioner's ongoing exposure to the substrate damage he repairs must be able to degrade his personal condition cumulatively across many seasons, distinct from the cost of any single act of repair.
His death, if it occurs while performing a repair, must be able to produce a different and better outcome for the world than the same repair performed by someone who lives.

A subordinate rank within a tiny, non-political, non-recruiting institution must be trackable as a real position with real relationships (a senior to answer to, peers to lose) even though the institution has no faction stats, no Domain Actions, and no seat at any political table.

The cumulative consequence of every other faction's warfare and Thread-disruptive activity anywhere on the peninsula must be able to reach him personally as an accumulating burden, without him ever having interacted with those factions.

His decades of specific field experience with a defined category of threat must make him mechanically superior at that category of action compared to someone without the experience, not merely narratively described as expert.
A player who reaches him must be able to have access gated by demonstrated Thread competence rather than by faction standing, reputation, or wealth -- none of which his institution recognizes.

UNCLEAR: the only detailed source for the state-machine map of his arc (analogous to the one that exists for his institution's chief) is a document that has since been moved out of the live source tree, so no season-level detail beyond one summary sentence is available to extract.

NPC-005.name: Sigrid Torsvald
NPC-005.one_line: A covert military-order operative whose official record and personal reality have diverged -- she does not officially exist, and neither does the Thread Sensitivity she has secretly developed.
NPC-005.ends_when: never explicitly stated; presumably her exposure and its institutional fallout, her death, or a resolution of the archive-connection arc -- none of which the source specifies as a defined final mechanical state.
who_acts: her covert order's commander (assigns missions, can override her)
the archive-owner she is still connected to
her order's overt leadership (would react to exposure)

rows.need: An act she performs must be able to leave no attributable trace back to her, her order, or her Crown when it succeeds cleanly -- full deniability as an achievable outcome, not merely a stated intention.

An act that goes partially wrong must be able to generate a persistent, accumulating institutional risk that is distinct from, and outlives, the scene in which it happened, and that risk must be able to cross a threshold that forces consequences later, in a different season, for a different reason.

Her private reputation among people who can never publicly credit her (fellow operatives, informants, a patron) must be trackable and consequential, on a track separate from any reputation she could have in ordinary faction life.

A perception or capability she secretly has (Thread Sensitivity) must be able to be true and mechanically active while remaining completely unknown to the institution she serves, with that institution's own rules treating mere discovery of the secret as automatically disqualifying, regardless of her competence or loyalty.

A refusal to accept a mission must be able to cost her standing even when her reasons (avoiding harm only she can perceive) are sound -- the institution's cost model cannot be sensitive to whether her private judgment was actually correct.

Her perception of the consequences of a mission must be able to diverge from her colleagues' and superiors' assessment of that same mission -- the identical event scored as a clean win institutionally and as a partial disaster by her personal standard.

A prior personal relationship formed years earlier (guarding an archive for someone she has since stayed connected to) must be able to resurface and pull her into a scene later, creating a genuine conflict between her covert obligations and that relationship.
If her covert status is exposed publicly, the consequence must convert what she gained secretly into an explicit, larger public loss, rather than simply erasing the secret gain.
Her overt institutional rank and her covert rank must be able to move independently -- advancement or disgrace in one must not automatically imply the same in the other.

NPC-010.name: Dalla Virke
NPC-010.one_line: An independent broker in illicit antiquities and information who profits from relationships no institution can requisition, and who has personally certified goods she did not know were dangerous.
NPC-010.ends_when: never explicitly named; presumably her exposure or recall event, or indefinite continuation.
who_acts: her family (can recall or replace her)
the Guild figure linked to her through the same exposure chain

rows.need: A non-faction, non-institutional actor must be able to hold and trade a resource (information, trust, access) that no faction's own action economy owns or produces -- a market that exists outside every faction's resource pools.

Information she sells must be able to be true, false, or fabricated, with the buyer unable to distinguish which in advance, and her incentive to fabricate must rise specifically when honest demand for information falls.

She must be discoverable, killable, buyable, or turnable by an outside actor as four textually distinct outcomes with different consequences for her network, not variations on one generic 'remove her' resolution.

Her personal judgment about a specific past transaction (vetting goods as safe and legitimate) must be able to be wrong in a way that is discoverable later and attributable specifically to her, not to an abstract 'the network' or 'the market.'

A revelation that damages her standing with one party (a partner learning she shields certain clients from her own family's operations) must be able to threaten her position with a different party (her family) whose interests and knowledge are entirely separate.

Her removal (replacement by someone with no local relationships) must be able to collapse benefits that other, unrelated actors were quietly relying on, in the same season, as a single cascading event rather than isolated losses each requiring its own trigger.

Trading in goods whose true dangerous nature is unknown even to the seller must be able to produce consequences later, when the nature becomes known, that attach retroactively to the original transaction rather than only affecting future trades.

UNCLEAR: reaching her for a player with no criminal or covert affiliation must be possible through some channel other than the adversarial 'discover a hostile intelligence asset' mechanism used to find brokers, since she is specifically framed as approachable rather than merely detectable.

NPC-012.name: Rikard Solberg
NPC-012.one_line: A foreign trade official whose homesickness has been unconsciously steering an entire nation's peninsula policy toward the one outcome -- Valorian stability -- that would let him go home.
NPC-012.ends_when: his recall, by his own nation or via a player-brokered genuine stability treaty, or indefinite continuation of the status quo.
who_acts: his home nation's central leadership (recalls him via its own strategic priorities)
the player (can offer him a real path to recall)
every faction his arms/intelligence/trade recommendations touch

rows.need: A single office-holder's personal, unstated motive must be able to measurably bias every decision he makes in that office, in one consistent direction, without him or his superiors recognizing the pattern.

His employer's institutional evaluation of him must be able to stay positive -- he is 'too valuable to recall' -- specifically because of the state of the world he is unconsciously prolonging, a closed loop between his output and his own continued posting.

A player who identifies his true motive must be able to offer him something categorically different from a bribe or a threat -- a real, verifiable path to recall -- and have that offer change his behavior, with the engine able to distinguish a genuine offer from a false one via his own judgment.
His own faction's strategic decision-making must be able to independently recall or replace him based on faction-scale conditions, entirely apart from any player action.

If he is replaced, his successor's behavior must differ measurably from his (more aggressive arms flows, sharper intelligence, harsher trade terms) as a direct consequence of removing his specific bias, not merely a new NPC with the same name.

His private, non-work relationships (his children, growing up without him) must be able to exist as a motivating fact even though they are physically absent from every scene he could appear in on the peninsula.
His institutional loyalty and the effect of his actions must be able to diverge permanently without him ever consciously betraying or defecting from his employer.

NPC-002.name: Maret Uln
NPC-002.one_line: A practitioner and intelligence operative whose lived perception of the population she surveils is eroding the professional discipline her work requires, and who is the sole named successor if her patron falls.
NPC-002.ends_when: never explicitly named as a terminus; presumably resolved only when she defects, successfully compartmentalizes, or her patron falls and she inherits.
who_acts: her patron (whose fall triggers her succession mode)
the population she surveils and sympathizes with

rows.need: Performing a Thread operation as part of ordinary intelligence work must cost the practitioner a persistent personal resource whose cost scales with the scale and type of operation performed, distinct from whether the operation succeeded.

As her personal condition degrades across a season, the range of actions available to her must narrow in a fixed, predictable order -- from full freedom down to forced withdrawal and crisis -- and that narrowing must override her institutional orders when the two conflict.

Her personal sympathy for a population she is ordered to act against must produce a measurable, repeatable delay or softening in her actions against that population, distinct from a single one-time refusal.

UNCLEAR: the two live canonical sources for her Thread Sensitivity disagree (one states roughly 50, the other states 35), and this is not a cosmetic discrepancy -- the two values sit in different tiers of the setting's own sensitivity banding, which changes how much strain her presence imposes on everyone close to her, every season.

A designated successor to a faction leader must exist as a real, trackable status -- with defined behavioral constraints relative to the current leader -- well before succession ever actually happens, not only as a rule that activates once on the leader's death.

If her patron is eliminated and she inherits leadership, a faction-level clock tied specifically to her predecessor's personal project must be able to reset to zero rather than simply transferring to her.

Her intelligence-gathering must be able to produce results that are qualitatively richer than ordinary reconnaissance -- direct experiential perception of substrate-level damage, not reported facts -- meaning what she knows about a target population must be represented as more than an abstract evidence value.
A season in which she takes no visible action against her own sympathies must still register as a choice with consequences (an opportunity cost to her faction), not as a null default outcome.

NPC-004.name: Sæmund Haelgrund
NPC-004.one_line: A Church Field Inquisitor whose "investigative instinct" is actually unrecognized Thread perception, deployed against heresy under conditions that can produce confident false convictions.
NPC-004.ends_when: never fully -- a single investigation ends when Reconstructed (successfully or not), but Sæmund's personal arc (undiscovered / defected / suppressed-and-degrading) persists indefinitely until the TS-revelation branch fires
who_acts: the PC or NPC attempting to Diagnose his Thread Sensitivity
a rival faction agent planting counter-evidence
the Church faction AI (the AP >= 3 deployment trigger)

rows.need: A completed investigation must be able to produce a plausible-but-wrong conclusion that its holder cannot distinguish from a correct one, and the holder must be able to act on it as true until later evidence or events contradict it.

A person must be able to possess a perceptual capacity he does not know he has, whose outputs he misattributes to a mundane cause (professional instinct), such that his real competence has a hidden, unacknowledged source.

A second person with the right capability must be able to run a targeted check ON Sæmund and learn something about him (his latent Thread Sensitivity) that he cannot detect in himself by any means available to him.

An institution must be able to make one of its investigators' authority to act vary by whose territory he is standing in -- full authority in home ground, conditional on another office-holder's formal request elsewhere, actively blocked in a third jurisdiction, and merely covert in unclaimed ground.
A third party must be able to spend a resource to plant false evidence into an investigation already in progress, degrading a conclusion that would otherwise have resolved correctly.

A party trying to stay hidden from an investigation must be able to spend ongoing effort, scene by scene, to raise the investigator's difficulty, with that difficulty lapsing the moment they are not present to maintain it.

Revealing this investigator's hidden nature must be able to remove him from his institution's service in a way that measurably degrades that institution's future capability in the same domain, not merely embarrass him personally.
A subordinate investigator's authority to pursue a sufficiently important target must be gated on a named superior's authorization, distinct from the subordinate's own competence or rank.

UNCLEAR: the sources give Sæmund the title 'Field Inquisitor' but never map it onto the Church's own formal Inquisitor rank ladder (Scribe / Junior / Inquisitor / Senior / Inquisitor-General), so what he is and is not personally authorized to do by rank -- versus by informal reputation as 'the Church's best investigator' -- is unspecified.

NPC-033.name: Kolbrun Thale
NPC-033.one_line: Crown's Spymaster and sole formal channel to the peninsula's informal intelligence-broker networks, operating on the edge of institutional propriety with a possibly-relevant hidden heritage.
NPC-033.ends_when: never specified -- she is a persistent office with no authored personal arc or end condition in the sources
who_acts: the settlement-layer intelligence broker she contacts

rows.need: An office must be able to be the sole official channel between an institution and an entire class of informal, deniable actors, such that removing that one office-holder severs the institution's access rather than merely weakening it.

A spymaster must be able to surface a hidden actor operating in a territory through sustained investigative effort against active concealment, at a cost that scales with how hard the concealed party is working to stay hidden.

On surfacing a hidden actor, the office-holder must be able to choose among structurally different dispositions of the discovery -- expose it, remove it, absorb it into her own network, or shelter it -- each carrying a distinct downstream consequence, rather than one universal 'resolve' outcome.

A formal advisor holding a position of institutional trust must be bound to secrecy about what her principal reveals to her in that capacity, as an obligation distinct from ordinary Disposition-gated information sharing.

A person's private, undisclosed heritage or sympathy must be able to bias which of her discoveries she reports faithfully and which she quietly softens or withholds, without the player or her principal being able to verify, in any single instance, which she did.

Two office-holders within the same institution whose remits abut (covert reach vs. doctrinal suspicion) must be able to carry a standing mutual wariness seeded by a specific past friction, coloring their dealings without either being able to simply overrule the other.
The office must be able to continue functioning (brokered deals still resolving, information still flowing) across a season in which the player takes no action involving her at all.

UNCLEAR: no formal ladder of subordinate field agents that Kolbrun personally commands is specified -- her only named organizational link is an informal, deniable relationship with a different faction's covert ladder (Löwenritter's Riskbreakers) -- so what happens when she needs to order rather than merely liaise is unstated.

NPC-083.name: Hedda Kronvald
NPC-083.one_line: Governor of Ehrenfeld, a five-adjacency geographic chokepoint, whose season is a closed loop of a mandatory faction Directive above her and independent settlement demands below her, both of which she cannot fully satisfy.
NPC-083.ends_when: not specified to conclude on its own -- the governorship ends only on removal, death, or promotion; the churn is designed to continue indefinitely otherwise
who_acts: the Provincial/Crown authority issuing the Directive
rival subnational factions maneuvering at the chokepoint
a retained clerk/deputy she may delegate to

rows.need: A governor must be able to spend a limited, renewing per-season budget across a menu of distinct administrative actions such that doing everything the settlement needs in one season is structurally impossible.

Each administrative action must be resolvable by more than one method, where the choice of method hands durable influence over the settlement to a different internal faction, rather than the raw magnitude of the action being the only thing that changes.

The governor's controlling authority must be able to issue a mandatory seasonal order she can comply with, negotiate down, or defy -- each option costing something different to the authority above versus the populace below -- with repeated defiance accumulating toward a threshold that eventually forces a reckoning.

The settlement itself must be able to generate demands (a dispute, a shortfall, an ambition) independent of and often in direct conflict with what the controlling authority ordered, such that the governor cannot satisfy both with the resources she has.

A governor's past rulings must be able to persist as durable marks on the settlement (a standing precedent, a grudge, an owed favor, a reputation) that bias future events, and a successor must inherit these rather than starting clean.

Named local actors under a governor's authority must be able to want incompatible things from EACH OTHER (not just from her), so that resolving one actor's grievance necessarily worsens another's, independent of any single choice she makes.

The settlement's overall pressure must rise on its own when demands go unmet and fall when the governor resolves them, so that an ignored settlement escalates and a well-managed one still keeps generating events rather than going permanently quiet.

UNCLEAR / structural: the mechanics this case depends on are themselves an unratified proposal explicitly gated on a settlement registry that does not yet exist in the engine, so it is unresolved whether any of the above is currently buildable as specified rather than only intended.

NPC-008.name: Peder Almstedt
NPC-008.one_line: The Ministry's Chief Parliamentary Clerk, whose custody of the sole surviving record of the founding settlement's terms lets him passively obstruct any reform that would alter it.
NPC-008.ends_when: never on its own -- the mechanism persists at the institutional level past his personal removal; only the Ministry's own dissolution would end it
who_acts: any leader or PC proposing a Parliamentary-structure-changing action (e.g. Lenneth, Baralta, Vaynard)
the Ministry as an institution (in his absence)

rows.need: A bureaucratic office-holder must be able to make any action that changes how the governing body itself functions strictly harder to accomplish, purely by holding the office, without an explicit hostile action or spent resource each time.
The same office-holder must simultaneously make one specific class of routine, stabilizing action easier or faster to accomplish, as the compensating flip side of the reform tax.

A person seeking institutional change must be able to overcome this obstruction only through one of a small, named set of costly alternatives -- winning him over directly, or removing him from office entirely -- with no free third route around it.

An office-holder must be able to hold institutional memory -- exact knowledge of an original founding agreement's terms -- that no other living actor holds, such that a proposal to alter those terms can be checked only against a standard nobody else can independently verify.

That sole-custody knowledge must be reusable to block multiple different actors' otherwise-unrelated reform proposals for the same underlying reason (each alters the terms he alone remembers), rather than needing a bespoke justification authored per proposer.

Removing the office-holder must erase the passive stabilizing benefit for a bounded period afterward, rather than the benefit persisting unaffected or the obstruction vanishing the instant it's needed.

The office, not the individual, must be the thing that actually persists -- Almstedt's specific removal should interrupt but not permanently end the obstruction/benefit mechanic, since the Ministry as an institution continues and can eventually refill the role.

UNCLEAR: one source places Almstedt as Hafenmark Parliament's own Standing-6 Senior Parliamentary Chair (mentoring Hafenmark's rank ladder), while the character registry files him under Crown (Ministry) faction -- whether he is a Crown-Ministry officer who happens to chair Hafenmark's Parliament, a cross-faction Ministry figure misfiled in one document, or something else is unresolved.

NPC-038.name: Arnlod Olafsson
NPC-038.one_line: Cardinal Justice, the Church's institutional head of the Inquisition, whose own hidden compromising connection is a standing liability to the entire apparatus he authorizes.
NPC-038.ends_when: his tenure ends on exposure-removal, pre-emptive removal, or a Grand Inquisitor succession event; otherwise never
who_acts: Sæmund Haelgrund and the rest of the Inquisitor ladder (subordinates)
a rival faction's agent pursuing exposure of his broker connection
the Church as an institution deciding whether to pre-emptively remove him

rows.need: An institution's investigative-and-punitive branch must have a single named superior whose sponsorship, approval, or authorization is a formal precondition for that branch's members to act above a defined severity or target-importance threshold.
That superior must be able to act against his own nominal superior's explicit instruction, at a real risk of outright failure (worse than compliance) and a cost attached even to success.

The superior's own hidden compromising connection must be discoverable by an external party through sustained, high-quality effort, and that discovery must remove him from office AND specifically degrade every subordinate operation under his branch for a bounded period -- not just embarrass him personally.

The institution must be able to choose, in advance of exposure, to sacrifice this office-holder pre-emptively at a smaller but permanent cost, giving it a genuine bet to make under uncertainty about whether exposure is coming.

The office's pattern of dispatching investigators must be able to fall unevenly on one population group even though the stated justification for each individual dispatch is doctrinal rather than ethnic, without the system anywhere forcing that disparity to be named or corrected.

This office-holder must be able to remain a purely institutional, non-directly-playable modifier under ordinary conditions, and only become a personally-acting, decision-making NPC once the institution falls below a stability threshold.

Once activated by institutional crisis, this office-holder must be able to direct his branch's investigative machinery inward, at a peer who nominally holds equivalent rank, not only outward at external heretics.

NPC-013.name: Aldric Tormann
NPC-013.one_line: The Fourth Cardinal (Prudence), whose aggressive tithe policy enriches the Church every season while quietly radicalizing the parishes it squeezes.
NPC-013.ends_when: never automatically -- only a fired Parish Revolt or a PC-driven resolution closes a given territory's version of the problem; his own tenure has no end condition tied to this behavior
who_acts: the parish leaders and populace in over-tithed territories
Confessor Himlensendt (nominal superior, if Tormann is ever ordered to stop)

rows.need: An office-holder must be able to take a repeatable seasonal action that reliably improves one faction-wide resource, with the improvement scaling by how many subordinate territories the office applies it to.

That same action must automatically and simultaneously degrade a slower-moving political resource in each affected territory, tracked separately per territory, with the accumulated damage converting to its faction-wide effect only at a periodic accounting point rather than immediately.

The political erosion this office-holder causes in a territory must be able to make that territory's population measurably more receptive to a rival, unaligned political movement, as an emergent side effect rather than a targeted action of his own.

The resource this office-holder generates must be spendable, elsewhere in the same institution, in a way that is thematically opposed to the harm his generation of it causes, without the system suppressing or resolving that standing contradiction.

Sustained harm from this office-holder's pattern in a given locality must be able to accumulate toward a distinct, nameable crisis event, rather than simply continuing to degrade a number indefinitely.

A player character must be able to intervene directly in this office-holder's tithe-collection pattern in one specific territory, altering the outcome there without requiring institutional authority over the Cardinal himself.

UNCLEAR: the registry's stated convictions (Order/Liberty) do not match the behavioral description of him as an OPTIMISER defined by aggressive wealth extraction, which reads closer to Order/Utility or Authority/Utility -- which pairing actually drives his Conviction-gated mechanics is unresolved.

NPC-007.name: Annika Feldhaus
NPC-007.one_line: The Guilds' economic representative, whose profit-maximizing stewardship has made the Guilds wealthy and politically irrelevant, and whose supply chain is unknowingly Thread-tainted.
NPC-007.ends_when: not specified to conclude -- resolves only through the (also open-ended) supply-chain revelation or recall arcs tied to Virke, or a direct exposure of Feldhaus's own half
who_acts: the internal Guild rival opposing her wealth focus
a PC investigator pursuing the Thread-touched goods lead
the Free-Masters examination committee she structurally benefits from

rows.need: A faction representative must be able to repeatedly grow one faction stat at the direct, automatic expense of a second faction stat every season, as her default behavior rather than a one-time choice offered to the player.

An economic actor's supply chain must be able to carry a hidden property that she has no way to detect given her own perceptual limits, such that she is materially responsible for a consequence she is structurally incapable of becoming aware of through her own effort.

Two separate economic actors who each independently built one half of the same tainted supply chain must have their exposure risks linked, such that revealing the taint through EITHER one damages BOTH, even though neither caused nor fully understands the connection.

A person must be able to hold two distinct organizational offices at once -- a cross-faction liaison seat and a rank within her home institution's own ladder -- each with its own advancement conditions, usable somewhat independently.

An internal rival within the same faction must be able to campaign, on an ongoing basis, for the opposite priority (collective standing over raw wealth) that this office-holder pursues, generating a live internal fork a player can take a side in.

A formal institutional gate she benefits from (an examination or credentialing process) must be able to carry a procedural, plausibly-deniable bias against a specific population, so that individual gatekeepers can point to 'the rules' rather than to her personal order, while she still benefits from the aggregate effect.

UNCLEAR: no threshold or trigger is specified for Feldhaus's own half of the supply chain becoming personally discoverable by investigation, unlike Virke's side which has an explicit cascading Domain Echo -- whether a player can target Feldhaus's half directly, or must always approach through Virke first, is unstated.

NPC-071.name: Torvi Heljason
NPC-071.one_line: Baralta's Legal Advisor in Hafenmark's Inner Council, specified almost entirely by a single extreme Precedent conviction with no authored goal, arc, or mechanical remit.
NPC-071.ends_when: UNCLEAR -- no arc, trajectory, or end condition is specified anywhere in the source; she is explicitly below the corpus's own stated minimum for individual arc tracking
who_acts: UNCLEAR -- no named counterpart is specified for the 'Knot rupture trigger' scene that references her

rows.need: A ruler's formal legal advisor must be able to give her frank counsel without that act of advising itself exposing her to personal consequence -- advising truthfully must be a protected kind of exchange, distinct from ordinary conversation.

An advisor whose sole articulated commitment is precedent and consistency must have every persuasive approach toward her scored differently depending on whether it appeals to established rule or to ad hoc circumstance, with the ad hoc approach yielding systematically less even when otherwise persuasive.

This advisor must be able to appear in a scripted relationship-rupture beat even though she has no authored personal arc, goal, or belief beyond her single conviction tag, and the scene must still be coherent.

UNCLEAR: the source never specifies what her office of Legal Advisor actually lets her DO mechanically -- block an illegitimate action, certify a treaty, merely offer non-binding opinion -- unlike Almstedt's explicit procedural-obstruction remit, hers is asserted by title alone.

UNCLEAR: no goal, ambition, leverage (wants/fears/secret), or relationship is specified for her anywhere in the corpus, despite the governance and relational frameworks elsewhere requiring exactly these fields to make an NPC scene-capable.

UNCLEAR: her single-conviction weight (0.70) is far higher than the roughly 0.5/0.2-0.3 split typical of other named NPCs, and it is not stated whether this reflects deliberate monomaniacal design or an unfilled second slot.

NPC-034.name: Gustav Linder
NPC-034.one_line: The Archbishop's Representative seated in the Crown's Inner Circle, whose formal permission is the sole legal conduit for Church heresy jurisdiction on Crown soil while his true loyalty answers to the Confessor.
NPC-034.ends_when: UNCLEAR -- no removal, exposure, or resolution condition is specified for the dual-loyalty tension itself; only the territorial-jurisdiction sub-mechanic (his permission request) resolves per-instance, each season it is invoked
who_acts: Almud Almqvist (nominal council principal and the gate-check target)
Crown Inner Circle peers who might notice divided loyalty
the Church's Inquisitor apparatus he is enabling access for

rows.need: A person embedded in one institution's inner circle must be able to be the single necessary formal conduit through which a SECOND institution's authority -- to which he actually answers -- can legally act inside the first institution's territory; without him, that authority does not exist there procedurally.

The institution he is embedded in must be able to refuse the request he is required to make on his true institution's behalf, under a specific named condition, so that his advocacy can fail even when he performs his function correctly.

A person must be able to sit in formal council for one institution while his substantive loyalty and reporting duty run to a different institution's leadership, such that the two institutions could in principle issue him contradictory instructions in the same season.

This person's confidentiality obligation to the council he sits on must be able to come into direct tension with his reporting obligation to his true master, such that honoring one at some point requires violating the other, with a real consequence attached to the choice.

A third party must be able to discover which of his two loyalties actually governed a specific past action of his, and that discovery must damage his standing in the institution he was seen to have subordinated, without necessarily being provable to the institution he was actually protecting.

This office-holder must be able to hold an automatic, standing hostile bias toward one category of person (Thread practitioners) that does not itself depend on which of his two loyalties is currently active, distinguishing 'things he does because he is a Church man' from 'things he does because he is favoring one master.'

UNCLEAR: no goal, ambition, or arc trajectory is authored for Gustav Linder anywhere in the corpus -- what his dual loyalty is FOR (surveillance of Crown policy? softening Crown actions toward the Church? preparing for a specific eventuality?) is unstated, so the tension his office permits has no content to resolve toward.

NPC-020.name: Almud Almqvist
NPC-020.one_line: A king whose season is entirely triage among pressures he cannot resolve, constrained more tightly by publicness than any private citizen would be.
NPC-020.ends_when: never automatically; his personal arc concludes only via one of several mutually exclusive branch conditions — reform, defensive consolidation, being overthrown by his own army, being consumed by a family tragedy, or his own death, at which point a different named person's case begins in his place
who_acts: the inner circle of appointed advisors
the rival duchess pressing her own claim

rows.need: A single leader must be able to face several independent, ongoing pressure sources in one season and only be able to substantively address a subset of them, with the unaddressed ones compounding rather than pausing.

A leader's own long-held private doubt about a policy he enforces must be able to persist for many seasons without forcing a decision, and that persistence must itself count as a consequential choice rather than a null state.

Actions taken in the leader's name by subordinates must be able to diverge from what he intended, through incompetence, institutional habit, or the subordinate's own judgment, and the leader must be able to learn of the divergence only after it happened.

A standing armed institution nominally loyal to the leader's position must be able to gradually reassess that loyalty in stages, driven by events the leader does not fully control, up to and including ceasing to execute his will.
The leader must be structurally unable to act on a piece of private knowledge or sympathy without incurring a cost that a lower-status person acting the same way would not incur.
A close advisor must be able to openly contradict or oppose the leader in a private setting at no cost to the advisor, while the same disagreement voiced publicly would cost the advisor standing.
The leader must be able to formally and publicly recognize another person's deed in a way that changes what that person may subsequently do, and this recognition must be withholdable, not automatic.

A crisis inside the leader's own family (an heir's death, a spouse's death, an heir's capture) must be able to fire unpredictably and reconfigure what the leader does for many subsequent seasons, visibly to every other actor.

A third party's multi-season campaign to eventually replace the leader must be able to proceed in parallel to his reign without the leader having any action that ends it outright, only ones that slow or manage it.

A future succession must be able to remain genuinely unsettled for the leader's whole reign, contested among parties with different bases of claim, none of which the leader can fully foreclose by simply naming an heir.

The leader's own perceptual or sensory state must be able to change through no action of his own, altering what he privately understands while his public role stays unchanged until he chooses, or is forced, to reveal it.

NPC-021.name: Arne Himlensendt
NPC-021.one_line: A religious institution's leader whose sincere private faith is the load-bearing pillar of a settlement he does not know is shaking.
NPC-021.ends_when: never automatically; his personal arc resolves via unchallenged doctrinal dominance, a private crisis of faith, or public confrontation and schism, and the institution's leadership itself ends only on his death, incapacity, or forced doctrinal crisis triggering a successor process
who_acts: the four subordinate arm-leaders (military, judicial, economic, scholarly)
the duchess pressing a claim on the throne
the secular territory that refuses his jurisdiction

rows.need: A religious institution's supreme leader must be able to publicly rule on doctrine in a way that materially shifts political-military measures elsewhere on the board.

A leader whose personal faith is intact must be able to have that faith privately challenged by presented facts, with a real chance his private conviction cracks while he continues performing his public role unchanged.

If the leader's private crack becomes known, the institutional damage must scale with how publicly it becomes known (rumor vs. proof vs. confession) rather than being a single binary discovered/undiscovered flag.

The leader must be able to face a decision where every theologically coherent answer available to him damages the institution in a different way, so there is no clean resolution regardless of which he picks.
A rival secular territory must be able to categorically deny this leader's coercive authority over its own residents, forcing him to negotiate or act covertly rather than command.

The leader must be able to delegate separate domains of institutional power (military, judicial, economic, scholarly) to different subordinate leaders who can each independently drift from his control, up to becoming more dangerous than he was.
A person's capacity for a certain kind of perception must be able to be permanently foreclosed by their institutional belief system, reachable again only through a shock external to ordinary play.
The same enforcement apparatus must be able to treat a follower differently purely based on which territory that follower is standing in when investigated.
The leader must be able to shield a subordinate's confidential counsel from any mechanical or reputational penalty even when that counsel directly contradicts his own stated position.

NPC-050.name: Inge Baralta
NPC-050.one_line: A duchess whose total personal command of her own duchy conceals that its survival without her is entirely unresolved, pressing a decades-long claim on a throne she cannot simply take.
NPC-050.ends_when: never automatically; her personal arc resolves via unchallenged rule of her own duchy, a forced turn to extralegal action, or being cast out of the religious institution entirely, and separately her pursuit of the throne resolves win, loss, or her death/removal triggering her own duchy's succession
who_acts: the church leader and his subordinate arm-leaders
her own inner council and legal advisor
the standing army's commander (a competing claimant)

rows.need: A leader must be able to build a multi-season positioning campaign toward a higher seat that only becomes attemptable once specific external conditions — the target seat's weakness AND a general instability threshold — are simultaneously true, so years of preparation can sit inert waiting on someone else's failure.
An overreaching attempt at the higher seat must be able to fail, cost the claimant standing, and be un-repeatable for a fixed cooldown period.

A leader's personal authority over her own institution must be able to be nearly absolute — her open disagreement with it costs her nothing — while the institution's survival without her personally remains unresolved, with no designated successor.

A claimant's success at seizing the higher seat must be conditioned on a third party's institutional state at the exact moment of the claim, so that an early, a middle, and a late attempt in the same campaign produce categorically different outcomes.

Taking the higher seat must be able to threaten the fracture of the claimant's home institution, contingent on a separate instability measure that keeps accumulating whether or not she is paying attention to it.

A rival institution must be able to refuse to recognize this leader's coercive authority over its own followers as a matter of stated principle, and that refusal must be a fact other actors can react to.

A leader who governs entirely through legalistic, precedent-bound methods must be able to become willing to act outside those methods once a specific named institutional failure occurs, and that shift must persist rather than reset the following season.

A theological or ideological innovation a leader personally originates must be able to spread its effects across the population she governs on a timescale much longer than the campaign, so it can exist as true worldbuilding without being an active mechanical variable.

NPC-052.name: Magnus Vaynard
NPC-052.one_line: A revolutionary duke whose authority is elective rather than absolute, whose private research risks transforming him, and whose fall could split his domain in two.
NPC-052.ends_when: never automatically; his personal arc resolves via unchecked scholarship, a personally transformative awakening, or being consumed by what he sought, and his leadership ends only on death, incapacity, or removal, triggering the succession/split outcome
who_acts: his intelligence operative and named successor-fallback
the movement leader who could back a rival successor

rows.need: A leader's personal, private research into a dangerous or forbidden knowledge domain must be able to advance his own capability while simultaneously risking a personal transformation he cannot fully control, checked probabilistically each time he uses it.

A confederated leader's authority must be able to be formally revocable by the collective body that grants it, through a multi-step process he cannot unilaterally block, requiring only a majority of his own senior subordinates.

A trusted subordinate acting in the leader's name must be able to carry a private, undisclosed conflict of loyalty that causes her to silently underperform one category of task, undetectable without independent investigation.

If this leader is removed from play, the identity of his successor must be able to remain genuinely undetermined among several qualified claimants, with the outcome capable of splitting his domain into two rival successor territories rather than resolving automatically to one heir.

A leader must be able to declare that no other party, including his own institution, can be trusted with the thing he protects, and act on that declaration in a way that isolates him from natural allies pursuing the same outcome.

A leader's public revolutionary ambition must be able to depend materially on the stability of the very system he intends to overthrow, without that dependency being visible to him or to the system's defenders.

An ideologically aligned peer with institutional access this leader lacks must be able to refuse to accelerate a shared goal on his preferred timeline, so agreement on diagnosis does not guarantee cooperation on method or pace.
A non-military, non-secret means of contesting a territory's cultural or religious alignment must be able to shift that alignment without transferring who controls the territory.

NPC-070.name: Lisbeth Ehrenwall
NPC-070.one_line: The commander of the crown's only standing army, whose institutional loyalty is a silent, gradually shifting professional judgment rather than a fixed allegiance.
NPC-070.ends_when: never automatically; concludes with either sustained loyalty through the campaign, an outright break in which the institution stops executing the ruler's will, or her removal transferring command with revised, harsher thresholds
who_acts: the liaison individual the internal struggle keys on
the wider military chain of command

rows.need: A standing military institution nominally loyal to a ruler must be able to progressively reassess that loyalty across several internal stages, driven by accumulating evidence of the ruler's failures, with no single season's evidence sufficient by itself to flip the institution against him.

The military leader assessing the ruler must be able to hold and act on a private professional judgment that is never voiced to the ruler as an accusation, yet still accumulates mechanically over time.

If the military leader is removed, whoever is next in the chain of command must be able to hold different priorities that redirect the institution's future actions in a concrete, different way than the original leader would have.

The military leader's own death or removal must be able to lower the institution's tolerance threshold for further provocation, so an already-tense situation escalates faster under new leadership than it would have under her.

A single named liaison individual must be able to function as the effective flashpoint of an internal power struggle between two institutions, because that individual's removal is what the underlying mechanism actually keys on, even though the nominal antagonists are larger bodies.
A diplomatic action by an outside party must be able to persuade the military institution to change its deployment posture without going through the ruler at all.

The military leader must be able to be personally reached by an appeal grounded in shared service or sacrifice in a way abstract political argument cannot, even though she is otherwise moved primarily by demonstrated consequences.

NPC-003.name: Yrsa Vossen
NPC-003.one_line: A movement leader whose authority exists entirely through relationship and visibility rather than any formal seat, and whose visibility is also her permanent vulnerability.
NPC-003.ends_when: never automatically while any presence remains; the movement formally ends only via reaching the highest institutional stage, total suppression with no remaining presence anywhere, or collapse once it has reached full institutional status
who_acts: a secondary, more operationally-focused movement leader
a reform-minded royal who could offer patronage
the church's field investigator conducting persecution
a rival faction's disgraced heir who could back the movement

rows.need: A person recognized as a movement's leader must be able to exert real influence and be targeted by opponents before any formal institutional seat or organizational structure exists for the movement at all, with that authority measured through relational and reputational quantities rather than a rank she occupies.

The leader's public visibility, which is the source of her influence, must be inseparable from the exact quality that exposes her to repeatable, institutional persecution — the game must not allow her to be influential while hidden.

A leader must be able to choose, season after season, between consolidating her base in fewer places or spreading it thinly across many, with that choice producing a measurably different vulnerability to a specific opposing institution's enforcement action.

If the leader is captured, killed, or discredited before the movement has achieved any formal institutional status, the movement's continuity must be able to remain genuinely ambiguous — a successor, a fragmentation, or a simple loss of coordination — rather than resolved by a procedure built for institutions that already have a formal leadership seat.

The movement's own base must be able to hold a genuine internal disagreement about whether to accept patronage from an established power or reject that power's legitimacy outright, without the leader's personal position resolving the disagreement for everyone who follows her.

An unincorporated movement must be able to acquire institutional standing incrementally — informal presence, then a single held settlement, then several, then a formal seat — with each threshold unlocking qualitatively different capabilities.

Even after the movement gains a formal seat, it must remain permanently excluded from a category of formal political action available to every incumbent institution, marking it as structurally second-class even once arrived.

A local population must be able to unilaterally shift its own governance to this movement's control the moment its existing governance completely collapses, without the movement's central leadership needing to have taken any action there that season.

NPC-032.name: Lenneth Almqvist
NPC-032.one_line: A queen consort with no independent action economy of her own, whose entire programme routes through persuading a man whose blockage is uncertainty, not disagreement — until an unpredictable event can make her sole ruler or kill her outright.
NPC-032.ends_when: never automatically while she remains queen consort; if she is elevated to sole ruler her case continues indefinitely as a new ongoing reign, and if she is instead the one killed her case ends immediately and permanently

Sustained private argument and demonstrated intellectual soundness from this person must be able to fail to move the decision-maker specifically because his blocking state is uncertainty rather than opposition, and the game must not treat sound argument as automatically persuasive against an uncertain target.

A person's capability in a specialized domain must be able to have a hard ceiling reachable through sustained legitimate effort, past which continued investment produces no further progress, with a categorically higher tier of that capability closed to her except through a wholly different pathway.

An external, unpredictable event unrelated to this person's own choices must be able to instantly convert her from an influence-only actor into the sole holder of supreme authority, with every downstream political relationship reconfiguring around the change in the same event.

The same unpredictable event, resolved differently, must instead be able to remove this person from play entirely, with the consequence of her death routing almost entirely through a different character's arc rather than her own.

Ascending to supreme authority through this path must be able to instantly and permanently redefine what the ruling institution stands for, flipping an ambient, privately-held policy uncertainty into an explicit, declared doctrine, rather than merely changing which person occupies the seat.

A previously unified protective institution must be able to fracture into an internal decision point purely as a consequence of who now holds supreme authority, with no change to its own formal chain of command.

A minor heir's declared loyalty must be able to transfer wholesale from one guardian to another the moment the first guardian is removed, without requiring the heir's own independent choice in that moment.

NPC-031.name: Torben Almqvist
NPC-031.one_line: A minor heir with no fixed political identity, whose eventual allegiance is won by whichever outside power invests in him fastest within a closing window, and who can be killed before it resolves.
NPC-031.ends_when: the contested-alignment phase ends at the window's close (or earlier, if a party wins outright) with a locked identity; his dependent status ends at maturation; his overall case ends only on death or the campaign's end
who_acts: whichever outside parties invest in him

The heir's relationship to whoever currently rules in his name must be able to range from voluntary total deference through open rivalry to an active, tracked contest for the same seat of power, determined by the accumulated quality of their relationship at the moment he matures.

The heir must be able to be killed by an unpredictable event that terminates his entire ongoing political arc and simultaneously reroutes a separate, compound set of consequences involving other characters and factions that have no bearing on anything he himself believed or did.

A foreign power with cultural or educational influence over an at-risk heir must be able to leverage that influence as a standing political threat even without ever acting on it, purely through its potential to alter what the heir will become.

The heir must be able to become a formal instrument of an external, rival power's diplomacy specifically when both the external power's own strength has crossed a threshold and the heir's personal relationship with the current regent has soured, rather than either condition alone being sufficient.
